newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-NIGHTWATCHMAN GILLESPIE SAVES SOUTH AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NIGHTWATCHMAN GILLESPIE SAVES SOUTH AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Jason Gillespie was the unlikely batting hero on Monday as South Australia salvaged a draw on the final day of their Sheffield Shield match against Western Australia.

The Australian pace bowler scored a career-best 58, occupying the crease for 268 minutes and facing 227 balls in his role as nightwatchman, as his side avoided the innings defeat which looked probable after Western Australia piled up 560 for eight declared in their first innings.

South Australia, needing 302 to avoid an innings defeat, resumed on 190 for three in the morning and batted all day to reach 381 for seven, forcing the West Australians to settle for nothing more than first-innings points.

Gillespie was dropped on 0 and 39, but displayed terrific powers of concentration and equally high stocks of courage to defy a desperate the home attack. He had the middle finger on his right hand taped and required pain-killing tablets after being struck by a delivery from Matthew Nicholson when he had made 41.

The impact loosened the 21-year-old's fingernail, but he will be fit for the third day test against the West Indies starting on Boxing Day. He was also struck a nasty blow on his left foot by a searing Nicholson yorker.
Gillespie's performance with the bat capped a memorable personal game. He claimed five wickets for just 64 runs from 30 overs in West Australia's innings.
